# Public sector and defense

## Scope

Applies when the change touches government services, public bodies, or defense contracts. Not when no government buyer, public body, or defense contract is involved; a commercial audit, such as SOC 2 or ISO/IEC 27001, is `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`'s. Neighbours: `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`, `aidd-team:accessible-ui`, `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`.

## Terms

- **ATO**: An authorization to operate: an agency official's acceptance of a system's risk.
- **Impact level**: FIPS 199's low, moderate, or high: it picks the control baseline.
- **Control baseline**: The SP 800-53 controls a system's impact level requires.
- **FIPS-validated module**: A cryptographic module with a CMVP certificate, not only an approved algorithm.
- **Continuous monitoring**: The ongoing evidence an ATO depends on.
- **CUI**: Controlled unclassified information, such as covered defense information, which DFARS 7012 makes a contractor safeguard.
- **Deemed export**: Releasing ITAR technical data to a foreign person, even inside the US.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-11-10 | The DFARS CMMC rule is in effect, starting Phase 1: a contract can require the CMMC status it names. | S9 |
| 2026-11-10 | CMMC Phase 2 begins a year after Phase 1 (32 CFR 170.3), adding Level 2 certification by a third-party assessor. Confirm the DoD's current phase first. | S9 |
| 2027-04-26 | ADA Title II (US): a state or local government of 50,000 people or more meets WCAG 2.1 AA on its web content and apps; a smaller one, or a special district, by 2028-04-26. | S7 |
| 2027-06-11 | FedRAMP stops accepting new Rev. 5 certifications; a new authorization follows the Consolidated Rules for 2026. | S3, S4 |
| 2028-12-31 | Existing Rev. 5 certifications remain active until at least this date, unless FedRAMP is otherwise directed. | S3 |

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| A change inside the boundary is assessed before it runs in production. | A new SaaS dependency, region, or data flow. |
| Cryptography runs in a validated module, in its approved mode. | A library's default outside FIPS mode. |
| Every control claim has current evidence. | A screenshot from last year's assessment. |
| ITAR technical data is reachable only by US persons. It stays on US systems unless it is end-to-end encrypted with a FIPS-validated module, as 22 CFR 120.54(a)(5) allows. | A CI runner, a support engineer, a backup, or a cloud region outside the allow-list. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | A government or defense system takes the compliance dimension (major) and keeps its evidence for the audit. Name the jurisdictions; `references/jurisdictions.md` holds the frameworks outside the US, and the identity assurance levels. | S1 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Defense work: CUI makes DFARS 7012 and CMMC apply, at the level the contract names; ITAR technical data stays with US persons. | S9, S10 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | A public web page or app meets WCAG 2.1 AA under ADA Title II for a US state or local government, and EN 301 549 with an accessibility statement in the EU. | S7 |
| Specify | Map the change to the NIST SP 800-53 controls it touches (US federal), or to the control set the jurisdiction names. | S2 |
| Specify | FIPS-validated cryptography named for any crypto change; new cryptography chosen with the post-quantum standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) in view. | S5, S6 |
| Specify | ITAR residency: the repository, CI runners, artifacts, logs, backups, and everyone with access are in the US and US persons; the config names the allowed regions and runners. | S10 |
| Implement | Logging and audit trails per the control baseline; no new cryptography outside the validated modules. | S2, S5 |
| Implement | A system holding CUI meets NIST SP 800-171 (Rev. 2 for a CMMC assessment); a cyber incident is reported to DoD on the DFARS 7012 clock. | S9 |
| Review | Control mapping and evidence complete; the POA&M updated for any accepted risk. | S2, S3, S4 |
| Roll out | Continuous-monitoring signals watched; the change record retained with the gate record. | S1, S4 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Control mapping | the touched controls (SP 800-53, or SP 800-171 for CUI) are named and reviewed | OSCAL (v1.2.3) component definitions and the SSP, validated with compliance-trestle (`uvx --from compliance-trestle==5.1.0 trestle validate -a`), or the team's control matrix | S2, S9 |
| Cryptography inventory | only FIPS 140-3 validated modules, and every algorithm listed for the post-quantum move | a CBOM (CycloneDX cryptographic assets) from the code, such as the CBOMkit sonar-cryptography plugin (1.7.0), checked against the allowed modules and algorithms | S5, S6, S8 |
| Audit log tests | every privileged action is logged with actor, time, and outcome | an integration test per privileged action that asserts the log entry's actor, time, and outcome, in the test commands | S2 |
| ITAR residency check | no ITAR-marked repository, artifact, or log is reachable from a runner, region, or account outside the allow-list | a policy-as-code check over CI runner labels, cloud regions, and repository access lists, in CI | S10 |

- From `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`: Dependency scan, Static analysis, Container scan and SBOM.
- From `aidd-team:accessible-ui`: Accessibility per state.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
